solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Poet, residing around Kew or itinerant, who doesn't commute

definitions.note: a relative clause standing for 'one who doesn't commute', a noun

indicators.note: to live around something is to enclose it, so one piece wraps another

parts.note: Homer, the Greek epic poet

indicators.note: an itinerant wanders from place to place, so these letters travel out of their order

parts.note: taken as written, letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A poet living near Kew Gardens, or wandering about, has no daily trip to the office.
explanation.walkthrough: HOMER is split around a rearrangement of KEW OR to give HOM-EWORK-ER. Kew is a district of west London known for its botanic gardens.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone based at their own house for their job has no daily journey to an office, which is what commuting means.

clue.text: Spiritual journey made by Juliet in the wake of husband Bill

indicators.note: a wake trails behind a boat, so whatever is in it comes after the rest

parts.note: H is the standard abbreviation for husband
a bill is an advertisement, shortened to ad
Juliet is J in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Juliet follows her husband Bill on a pilgrimage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the wake of' puts Juliet after the other two pieces. 'Bill' looks like the husband's name, but it is a separate piece meaning a poster or advert.
explanation.definitionFit: The hadj is the pilgrimage to Mecca that every able Muslim should make, a religious trip.

clue.text: Press the wrong buttons at first, mocking one's face

indicators.note: what comes at first is the opening, so only the initial letter of the next word is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of the word
one is I, and 's is short for is, so 'one's' reads as I + S
dial is slang for a face

explanation.surface: Someone hits the wrong buttons, then laughs at their own face.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One's' looks possessive but is read as 'one is', giving I and S. Dial is old British slang for a face.
explanation.definitionFit: To misdial a phone is to key in an incorrect number by pushing the wrong keys.

clue.text: Cocktail with rum certain to lift Welshwoman

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifting something turns it upside down so it reads bottom to top
rum here means odd or strange, so these letters come out in a peculiar order

parts.note: taken as written, letters to be rearranged
certain means sure
Sian is a common Welsh girl's name

explanation.surface: A cocktail containing rum is bound to cheer up a woman from Wales.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rum' looks like an ingredient of the drink, but it is the signal that WITH is to be rearranged; a White Russian has no rum in it.
explanation.definitionFit: A White Russian is a mixed drink of vodka, coffee liqueur and cream, so it is a named cocktail.

clue.text: What may drop crumbs down pullover?

parts.note: surface reading: something messy shedding crumbs while being eaten
setter's reading: a bread bun shedding crumbs down the throat-and-collar area of the body

explanation.surface: Someone asks what might shed crumbs all down a jumper.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer into its two halves: a bread bun, and the part of the body crumbs fall down. A pullover is a jumper, a knitted top.
explanation.definitionFit: This style of knitted sweater has a high collar folded over at the throat, so it names a kind of jumper.

clue.text: Politician's superior memory apparent during recording

indicators.note: something seen during another thing shows up in the middle of it, so one piece sits inside another

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record
U means upper-class or superior
ROM is read-only memory in a computer

explanation.surface: A politician turns out to have an excellent memory when being taped.
explanation.walkthrough: U for upper-class is an old British label for posh usage. The 's after the definition reads as 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A Euro-MP is a member of the European Parliament, an elected lawmaker and so a politician.

clue.text: Desert still lacking moisture on the east side

indicators.note: lacking means going without, so a letter is taken away

parts.note: still means quiet
the east side of a word written across is its right-hand end, its last letter

explanation.surface: A desert stays dry with no water on its eastern edge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Desert' wants to be the dry landscape, but it is the verb, to abandon. The last letter of 'moisture' is removed from QUIET.
explanation.definitionFit: To desert a post or a cause is to abandon it, to leave and give up on it.

clue.text: Odd students with university residing in squalor, centrally

indicators.note: to live inside something is to be enclosed by it, so one group of letters goes within another
centrally points to the core of a word, so only its middle letters are used

parts.note: the middle three of the word's seven letters
the NUS is the National Union of Students
U is the standard abbreviation for university

explanation.surface: Strange students at a university living in grim conditions.
explanation.walkthrough: The National Union of Students is the UK's national student body. 'Odd' looks like it describes the students but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Odd and unusual are synonyms for something out of the ordinary or strange.

clue.text: Recollected story about ancient plaything

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece encircles another
re-collected means gathered again, so these letters are picked up and set down in a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written, letters to be rearranged
an ancient is an old person, an oldie

explanation.surface: Someone remembers a tale about an antique toy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recollected' reads as remembered, but split as re-collected it calls for rearrangement. 'Ancient' is a noun here, an old person.
explanation.definitionFit: A miniature figure of a military man is a classic children's toy, something to play with.

clue.text: Plant trellis relocated during home improvements

indicators.note: during means in the course of, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: DIY, do-it-yourself, is home improvement work

indicators.note: moved to new places, so these letters change position

parts.note: taken as written, letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A climbing plant's trellis is moved during some home renovation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant' wants to be something growing up the trellis; it is an industrial works.
explanation.definitionFit: A plant can mean a factory, and a distillery is a factory where spirits such as whisky are made.

clue.text: Landing area reached using guide over the airwaves

indicators.note: something broadcast over the airwaves is heard rather than read, so go by sound

parts.note: a key is a guide, as to a map or puzzle

explanation.surface: An aircraft finds its landing strip with help from radio guidance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Landing area' suggests an airstrip, but it is where boats land.
explanation.definitionFit: A quay is a wharf where ships tie up and passengers come ashore, so a place for landing.

clue.text: Bulldog can stand for this new trainer with bait (edge of gammon)

indicators.note: something made new is remade, so these letters form a fresh arrangement

parts.note: taken as written, letters to be rearranged
taken as written, letters to be rearranged

indicators.note: an edge is the very start of something, so only the first letter is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A dog trainer lures a bulldog with a scrap of gammon, a kind of ham.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface looks like obedience training; really the bulldog is a national emblem.
explanation.definitionFit: The British bulldog is a traditional symbol of the nation, so the dog can represent the country.

clue.text: Judge the writer's style of music

parts.note: J is the abbreviation for judge
the writer is 'I', and 'the writer's' reads as I've, I have

explanation.surface: A judge assesses an author's musical style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The writer's' looks possessive but is read as 'the writer has', which contracts to I'VE.
explanation.definitionFit: Jive is a lively swing-era genre of jazz and the dance done to it.

clue.text: Ace Italian boss?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the best, the top one
second meaning: Italian for 'number one', a name for the person in charge

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the second meaning works by translation: the phrase is Italian, and the boss is number one.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian phrase for 'number one' is used in English for the best thing or the most important person.

clue.text: One poaches, say, very French old-fashioned starter in restaurant

parts.note: très is French for very
passé means out of date

indicators.note: a starter is what comes first, so only the opening letter is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A chef poaching eggs in a very French, outdated way as a restaurant starter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poaches' and 'starter' set up a kitchen; the poaching is illegal hunting, and 'say' marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: A poacher goes onto private land without permission to hunt, which makes them an intruder on property.

clue.text: Again introduce the Ibizan with skimpy lewd clothing

indicators.note: skimpy means cut short, so the word loses its final letter
clothing covers what it is worn over, so one piece wraps around another

parts.note: lewd is raunchy, here trimmed of its last letter
el is 'the' in Spanish, the language of Ibiza

explanation.surface: A nightclubber from Ibiza is reintroduced wearing revealing, saucy clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Skimpy' looks like it describes the clothes but trims RAUNCHY; 'clothing' is a verb, dressing EL in it.
explanation.definitionFit: To relaunch a product is to bring it out to the public a second time, introducing it anew.

clue.text: Legendary sports chiefs close to club watch display

parts.note: the FA, the Football Association, runs English football

indicators.note: the close of something is its end, so only the final letter is kept

parts.note: the final letter of the word
an LED display shows the time on a digital watch

explanation.surface: Famous sporting bosses near a club look on at some show.
explanation.walkthrough: The FA is the governing body of English football. 'Watch display' is a digital readout, not something to look at.
explanation.definitionFit: Fabled and legendary are synonyms, both describing something famous and told of in stories.

clue.text: Kitty and Paul arranged basement for secret fling

parts.note: Kitty is a pet name for a cat

indicators.note: arranged means put in a new order, so these letters are reordered

parts.note: taken as written, letters to be rearranged

indicators.note: a basement is the lowest level, and in a down clue the bottom letter is the last one

parts.note: the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: Kitty and Paul set up a cellar hideaway for a clandestine affair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fling' wants to be a brief affair in this picture, but it is the verb, to hurl.
explanation.definitionFit: To catapult something is to hurl it with force, as a slingshot does, which is to throw it.

clue.text: Salvation Army with good person holding case for flute that makes most sound

definitions.note: a clause meaning 'most sound', a superlative adjective

indicators.note: holding something is keeping it inside, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: SA is the abbreviation for the Salvation Army

indicators.note: a case is the outside of something, so only the outer letters are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters of the word
a saint, abbreviated ST, is a good person

explanation.surface: A Salvation Army band member clutching the flute case that makes the loudest noise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' wants to mean noise, but here it means secure or reliable; the Salvation Army and saint together hold the flute's outer letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Sound can mean secure and free of risk, so the most sound option is the least dangerous one.

clue.text: Fancy fruit conveyed when rambling?

parts.note: a fig is a fruit

indicators.note: rambling talk is loose and slurred, so words are judged by how they come out in speech

parts.note: conveyed in the sense of meant, signified

explanation.surface: Some posh fruit carried along on a country walk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fancy' looks like an adjective for the fruit, but it is a noun, a flight of imagination. Run 'fig meant' together carelessly and you get the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A fancy is something imagined, and a figment is likewise an invention of the mind.

clue.text: Local worker stopped by copper gets a grilling

parts.note: a local is a pub, a bar

indicators.note: something stopped by an obstacle has it plugged inside, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: a worker bee
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: A local labourer is stopped by a police officer and given a hard questioning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' and 'grilling' suggest police interrogation; the copper is the metal and the grilling is cooking. A local is British slang for a neighbourhood pub.
explanation.definitionFit: A barbecue is a meal or event where food is cooked over an open flame on a grill.

clue.text: Opening reading perhaps in church on sin

indicators.note: in a down clue, one thing on another sits above it, so the first group comes before the second
in means inside, so one piece is placed within another

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
reading is one of the three Rs, abbreviated R
a vice is a sin

explanation.surface: A first reading at a church service about wrongdoing.
explanation.walkthrough: The three Rs are reading, writing and arithmetic, so 'reading perhaps' is R. 'Opening' looks like an adjective for the reading; it is a noun, a gap.
explanation.definitionFit: A crevice is a narrow crack or gap in rock or a wall, so an opening.

clue.text: Insular offshore location's funds protecting Greek character

indicators.note: to protect something is to surround and shield it, so one piece wraps another

parts.note: an ISA is an Individual Savings Account, a UK tax-free fund
chi is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: Money held in an offshore island tax haven shields a Greek.
explanation.walkthrough: An ISA is a British tax-free savings account. 'Offshore' and 'funds' suggest tax havens, but the location is literally an island.
explanation.definitionFit: Ischia is an island in the Bay of Naples, a place surrounded by sea off the Italian coast.

clue.text: Main energy supplied by electrical company once going to Welsh city (not SW)

indicators.note: not marks letters to be left out, so they are removed

parts.note: AEG was a German electrical-goods manufacturer, now largely just a brand name
E is the symbol for energy
Swansea is a city on the south coast of Wales
taken as written, the letters to remove

explanation.surface: The bulk of power came from a former electricity firm supplying a Welsh city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Main' looks like 'chief', but the main is an old word for the sea. SW, south-west, is also where Swansea lies.
explanation.definitionFit: The main is a poetic term for the open ocean, and the Aegean is the arm of the Mediterranean between Greece and Turkey.

clue.text: Football team back keeps live animal

indicators.note: keeping something means holding it inside, so one piece goes within another
going back means running the wrong way, so the letters read right to left

parts.note: a football team has eleven players, XI in Roman numerals
to live is to be, to exist

explanation.surface: A football team's defender holds on to a living creature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' looks like a defender, a position on the team, but it signals reading XI the other way round.
explanation.definitionFit: The ibex is a wild mountain goat with long curved horns, so a kind of animal.

clue.text: Kiss by mistletoe's primarily when?

parts.note: X is the kiss written at the end of a letter

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so only the opening letter is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of the word
as can mean when, as in 'as I left'

explanation.surface: A question: at what time of year do people kiss under the mistletoe?
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: the answer to the question is the season when kissing under mistletoe is customary.
explanation.definitionFit: Hanging mistletoe and kissing beneath it is a festive custom of the December holiday season.

clue.text: In the past, one worshipped around African city

indicators.note: turned around means facing the other way, so the letters read backwards

parts.note: Zeus, king of the Greek gods, was worshipped in ancient times

explanation.surface: Someone once worshipped near a city in Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One worshipped' reads as a person praying, but it is the one who was worshipped, a god.
explanation.definitionFit: Suez is a port city in Egypt at the southern end of the canal named after it.

clue.text: I could break mum's heart, suffering ailment

indicators.note: something broken is smashed into bits that can be put back in a different order

parts.note: taken as written, letters to be rearranged
taken as written, letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A child fears breaking their mother's heart, she already being unwell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heart' looks like a selection signal for the middle of 'mum', but the whole word joins the letters to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Rheumatism is a painful condition of the joints and muscles, so a medical complaint.

clue.text: Regulars inside crazy about one-time posh venue

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece encircles another
regular letters are every other one, taken here from within the word

parts.note: the second and fourth letters
I is the Roman numeral for one
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Regular guests go mad over a once fashionable venue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One-time' looks like 'former', but it splits into two pieces. The Ritz is a famous luxury hotel in London.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ritz is a byword for luxury: a grand, upmarket London hotel where the smart set gather.

clue.text: Miss appearing before head for reckless behaviour

parts.note: to miss is to want, to feel the lack of
a performer appearing is on, as on stage
a ness is a headland

explanation.surface: A young woman goes before a headteacher for bad conduct.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Miss' and 'head' suggest a pupil sent to the head; head is a headland, a ness, as in Loch Ness's neighbouring place names. 'Before' just orders the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Wantonness means unrestrained, careless or immoral conduct, done without regard for consequences.
